   "id": "36b1ac60",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Mode profiles from the numeric model\n",
    "\n",
    "The `SingleLayerNumeric` class calculates the spin-wave (SW) dispersion by numerically\n",
    "diagonalizing a system matrix, following Tacchi et al.\n",
    "[[*Phys. Rev. B* **100**, 104406 (2019)]](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.100.104406).\n",
    "Besides the eigenfrequencies, it also returns the eigenvectors, which tell us how the dynamic\n",
    "magnetization is distributed across the film thickness, i.e. the *mode profiles*.\n",
    "\n",
    "In the [basic dispersion example](dispersion_relation_basic.ipynb), we saw that the modes of a\n",
    "100 nm thick NiFe film avoid crossing each other.  Here we look at the same film and ask what\n",
    "happens to the modes at these avoided crossings."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "82a80f96",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-10T09:13:58.253213Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-10T09:13:58.252205Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-10T09:14:00.989086Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-10T09:14:00.987068Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from matplotlib.lines import Line2D\n",
    "import SpinWaveToolkit as SWT"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "dffdeea9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We use the same parameters as in the basic example: an in-plane magnetized film in the\n",
    "Damon-Eshbach (DE) geometry ($\\mathbf{k} \\perp \\mathbf{M}$).  The parameter `N` sets the number\n",
    "of thickness modes in the basis, i.e. the size of the system matrix ($2N \\times 2N$).  Only the\n",
    "lowest modes are accurate, so we take a few more than we want to look at."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "97091dc5",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-10T09:14:00.991120Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-10T09:14:00.991120Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.278669Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.276535Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 500x350 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mat = SWT.NiFe\n",
    "d = 100e-9  # (m) layer thickness\n",
    "Bext = 50e-3  # (T) external magnetic field\n",
    "theta, phi = np.pi/2, np.pi/2  # (rad) in-plane M, DE geometry\n",
    "k = np.linspace(0, 25e6, 200) + 1  # (rad/m) SW wavenumber\n",
    "N = 6  # number of thickness modes in the basis\n",
    "nmodes = 3  # number of modes to plot\n",
    "\n",
    "sln = SWT.SingleLayerNumeric(Bext, mat, d, k, theta, phi, N=N)\n",
    "w, v = sln.GetDispersion()  # eigenfrequencies and eigenvectors\n",
    "f = w/(2e9*np.pi)  # (GHz)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig = plt.figure(figsize=(5, 3.5))\n",
    "for n in range(nmodes):\n",
    "    plt.plot(k*1e-6, f[n], label=f\"branch {n}\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(r\"wavenumber $k$ (rad/µm)\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(r\"frequency $f$ (GHz)\")\n",
    "plt.legend(loc=\"lower right\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f1007c9c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The modes are sorted by frequency, so we call them *branches*.  The steep DE mode starts as\n",
    "the lowest branch, but soon runs into the first perpendicular standing spin wave (PSSW) at\n",
    "about 1 rad/µm and into the second one at about 8 rad/µm.  Instead of crossing, the modes\n",
    "hybridize and the DE character is handed over from branch 0 to branch 1 and then to branch 2.\n",
    "The mode profiles will show this.\n",
    "\n",
    "## From eigenvectors to mode profiles\n",
    "\n",
    "The eigenvectors `v` have the shape `(2*N, N, len(k))`: for each branch and wavenumber, they\n",
    "contain the amplitudes of the $N$ thickness modes of the basis.  For the unpinned boundary\n",
    "conditions (the default `boundary_cond=1`), these are $\\cos(n \\pi z / d)$, where the uniform\n",
    "mode ($n = 0$) is weighted by $1/\\sqrt{2}$.  The even entries (`v[0], v[2], ...`) belong to the\n",
    "out-of-plane (OOP) and the odd entries (`v[1], v[3], ...`) to the in-plane (IP) component of\n",
    "the dynamic magnetization:\n",
    "\n",
    "$$m_\\mathrm{OOP}(z) = \\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} v_{2n}\\, \\psi_n(z), \\qquad\n",
    "m_\\mathrm{IP}(z) = \\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} v_{2n+1}\\, \\psi_n(z), \\qquad\n",
    "\\psi_n(z) = \\frac{\\cos(n \\pi z / d)}{\\sqrt{1 + \\delta_{n0}}}.$$\n",
    "\n",
    "The sign of an eigenvector is arbitrary, so we choose it such that the OOP component is\n",
    "positive where it is largest."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "2fdacc14",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.281694Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.281694Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.293654Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.291641Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def mode_profile(v, z, d):\n",
    "    # OOP and IP profiles for eigenvectors `v` with shape (2*N, ...)\n",
    "    n = np.arange(v.shape[0]//2)\n",
    "    psi = np.cos(np.outer(n, z)*np.pi/d)  # basis functions, (N, Nz)\n",
    "    psi[0] /= np.sqrt(2)\n",
    "    oop = np.einsum(\"n...,nz->...z\", v[0::2], psi)\n",
    "    ip = np.einsum(\"n...,nz->...z\", v[1::2], psi)\n",
    "    # fix the arbitrary sign: OOP positive at its maximum\n",
    "    imax = np.argmax(np.abs(oop), axis=-1)[..., np.newaxis]\n",
    "    sign = np.sign(np.take_along_axis(oop, imax, axis=-1))\n",
    "    return sign*oop, sign*ip\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "z = np.linspace(0, d, 101)  # (m) coordinate across the thickness"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a32ed19b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Profiles at selected wavenumbers\n",
    "\n",
    "Let's look at all three branches at a small, an intermediate and a large wavenumber.  Solid\n",
    "lines are the OOP and dashed lines the IP components."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "11eb20b7",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.295659Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.295659Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.622970Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.620971Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x400 with 3 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "k_sel = [3e6, 12e6, 24e6]  # (rad/m)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(8, 4), sharey=True)\n",
    "for ax, ks in zip(axs, k_sel):\n",
    "    i = np.argmin(np.abs(k - ks))\n",
    "    oop, ip = mode_profile(v[:, :nmodes, i], z, d)\n",
    "    for n in range(nmodes):\n",
    "        line, = ax.plot(z*1e9, oop[n], label=f\"branch {n}\")\n",
    "        ax.plot(z*1e9, ip[n], \"--\", color=line.get_color())\n",
    "    ax.set_title(f\"$k$ = {k[i]*1e-6:.0f} rad/µm\")\n",
    "    ax.set_xlabel(r\"$z$ (nm)\")\n",
    "    ax.axhline(0, color=\"k\", lw=0.5, ls=\"-\")\n",
    "axs[0].set_ylabel(\"amplitude ()\")\n",
    "axs[0].add_artist(axs[0].legend(loc=\"lower left\"))\n",
    "styles = [Line2D([], [], color=\"k\", ls=ls) for ls in (\"-\", \"--\")]\n",
    "axs[0].legend(styles, [\"OOP\", \"IP\"], loc=\"lower right\")\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "eb1d6bcc",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "At 3 rad/µm, branch 1 is the DE mode: its amplitude is almost uniform across the film, while\n",
    "branches 0 and 2 are the first and second PSSW with one and two nodes.  At 24 rad/µm, the DE\n",
    "mode has moved to branch 2, and its IP component is concentrated at one of the surfaces\n",
    "(here $z = 0$) – the well-known surface character of DE waves at large $kd$.  Generally, the IP\n",
    "amplitude is larger than the OOP one, as the precession in an in-plane magnetized film is\n",
    "elliptical.\n",
    "\n",
    "## Transitions of the mode character\n",
    "\n",
    "Finally, we calculate the profiles for all wavenumbers at once and plot the precession\n",
    "amplitude $m_\\mathrm{IP}^2 + m_\\mathrm{OOP}^2$ across the thickness for each branch.  The\n",
    "eigenvectors are normalized as $\\sum_j v_j^2 = 1$, i.e.\n",
    "$\\frac{2}{d}\\int_0^d (m_\\mathrm{IP}^2 + m_\\mathrm{OOP}^2)\\,\\mathrm{d}z = 1$ for every branch and\n",
    "wavenumber, so a larger maximum reflects a stronger localization and a higher ellipticity of\n",
    "the precession."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "b895e274",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.626087Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-10T09:14:01.626087Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-10T09:14:02.218695Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-10T09:14:02.218695Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x400 with 4 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "oop, ip = mode_profile(v[:, :nmodes], z, d)  # shape (nmodes, len(k), Nz)\n",
    "amp = oop**2 + ip**2\n",
    "vmin, vmax = np.min(amp), np.max(amp)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(8, 4), sharey=True,\n",
    "                        layout=\"constrained\")\n",
    "for n, ax in enumerate(axs):\n",
    "    mesh = ax.pcolormesh(k*1e-6, z*1e9, amp[n].T, shading=\"auto\",\n",
    "                         vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)\n",
    "    ax.set_title(f\"branch {n}\")\n",
    "    ax.set_xlabel(r\"$k$ (rad/µm)\")\n",
    "axs[0].set_ylabel(r\"$z$ (nm)\")\n",
    "fig.colorbar(mesh, ax=axs, label=r\"$m_\\mathrm{IP}^2 + m_\\mathrm{OOP}^2$ ()\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "12dc209f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The avoided crossings at about 1 and 8 rad/µm appear as abrupt changes of the profiles: the\n",
    "nearly uniform DE profile jumps from branch 0 to branch 1 and then to branch 2, where it\n",
    "gradually localizes at the surface $z = 0$.  The PSSW profiles with nodes are handed down to the\n",
    "lower branches in turn."
   ]
  }
 ],
